findings.title: Discrete enumeration does not isolate posterior-overlap error
findings.location: Section3 p4; Section6.1 p7; AppendixD.1 p21 and Figure3 p22
findings.source_claim: Discrete comparison estimates error only due to posterior overlap and supports the low-error cost of flexible multivariate Bayesian discovery. The paper also states an expectation of higher error due to continuous-relaxation optimization; this tentative comparison is not treated as a failed universal claim. The Major finding is anchored to the explicit overlap-only isolation.
decisive_evidence: D.1 uses a collapsed variational lower bound, 200 inducing points, optimized latent-variable variational parameters, nonconvex Adam/BFGS and10 best-bound restarts.
Figure3 changes the error metrics when restart budget changes while the tested datasets/model family are unchanged.
Enumerating candidate graphs does not eliminate graph-dependent variational gaps or incomplete optimization; the compared procedures also differ in kernels and approximation.
findings.assumptions_and_scope: The finding concerns identification by the described experiment. It does not assert a numerical counterexample to the conditional theory, an exact-score reversal for the published datasets, or a changed true Bayes-risk value.
findings.dependency: Section3 explicitly cites Section6.1 as the empirical justification that the chosen flexible multivariate model class has a low error probability. The explicit overlap-only isolation is unsupported by the actual approximate procedure, directly affecting this core inferential contribution. The continuous/discrete comparison does not provide an error-source decomposition; its tentative expectation of higher continuous-optimization error is preserved and is not treated as a failed universal claim.
counterevidence: Definition3.1 permits a general score, so measured approximate-procedure error remains meaningful.
Variational approximation and restart sensitivity are openly disclosed.

Low observed error may support practical usefulness; under matched generative distribution and classification loss, procedure population risk can upper-bound optimal Bayes risk, without identifying the observed error decomposition.

repair.statement: Describe the discrete and continuous results as complete approximate-procedure performance and remove the overlap-only isolation interpretation. Preserve the tentative expectation of higher error from continuous-relaxation optimization without asserting that the comparison quantifies or isolates that contribution.
repair.verification: Claim-to-design dependency and ELBO-gap reasoning inspected; source Figure3 checked directly. No empirical reanalysis or author-code execution.
repair.remaining: Quantitative source decomposition needs controlled matched comparisons or validated marginal-likelihood/ranking bounds; actual contributions unmeasured.
